Why do you need a token?

In the past, developers could connect their computer's terminal to GitHub using their standard account username and password. However, for security reasons, GitHub no longer allows password authentication for command-line operations.

Today, to interact with GitHub from your terminal (or a Coursera lab environment) over HTTPS, you must use a Personal Access Token (PAT) . A PAT functions as a highly secure, temporary password. You can control exactly what the token is allowed to access (its "scopes"), and you can revoke it at any time to keep your account safe.

Note on Software Images: This reading contains software screengrab images. While GitHub's appearance often evolves with continual updates, the core functionalities and menu paths covered in this reading will remain applicable.

Generate a Personal Access Token

Let's set up your token so you can successfully complete your upcoming lab exercises.

Step 1: Log in to GitHub.com.

Step 2: Click on your profile icon in the top right corner of the screen and select Settings from the dropdown menu.

Step 3: On the Settings screen, scroll all the way down the left-hand sidebar and click Developer settings .

Step 4: On the left sidebar, click Personal access tokens to expand the menu, and then click on Tokens (classic) . Finally, click the Generate new token button on the right and select Generate new token (classic) .

Step 5: On the setup page, enter a descriptive Note (e.g., "Coursera Labs") so you remember what this token is for. Under Expiration , you can set a time limit or select No Expiration if you wish to manually revoke it later.

Step 6: Under the Select scopes section, you must define what this token is allowed to do. For this course, you must check two specific boxes:

  1. Check the repo box (this grants full control of repositories).

  2. Scroll down to the admin:org section and check the read:org box (this is required to access the Coursera lab environments).

Step 7: Scroll to the bottom of the page and click the green Generate token button.

Step 8: Your token is now generated! You must copy this token immediately. Click the copy icon next to the token string and paste it somewhere safe (like a temporary notepad file). For security reasons, once you leave or refresh this page, GitHub will hide the token forever.

(Note: If you lose the token, don't panic. You can simply delete the old one and generate a new one). [Screenshot: Copy and save the token]

Accessing Repositories (How to Use Your Token)

Now that you have your token, you can clone and push to repositories over HTTPS.

When you want to download a project, navigate to the repository on GitHub, click the green Code button, make sure the HTTPS tab is selected, and copy the web URL.

Using the Token in the Terminal: When you go to your terminal and run a command that interacts with GitHub (such as git clone or git push), the terminal will pause and ask for your credentials:

  1. Username: Enter your GitHub username.

  2. Password: Do NOT type your actual GitHub password. Paste the Personal Access Token you copied in Step 8 and press Enter.

( Terminal Tip: When pasting your token into a command-line terminal, the cursor will not move, and no stars or characters will appear on the screen. This is a standard security feature! Just paste it once and press Enter).
